# MidwayBuyer

<!-- generated by scripts/render.mjs from data/ ; do not edit -->

Stable application-facing contract that routes each request to its saved Engine.

**Address**: [`0x1fb010F5C4A569DBD1CB6bD14b189a53ADdD49A8`](https://evm.now/address/0x1fb010F5C4A569DBD1CB6bD14b189a53ADdD49A8?chainId=1)
**Source**: `src/midway/MidwayBuyer.sol`

| `claimEpochRewards(uint256,uint256[])` | Claims closed-epoch purchaser rewards. Restricted to the request's recorded account: the rewards land on `purchaserRewardRecipient` either way, so a third-party claim consumes the epoch out of band and strips whatever attribution the account performs around its own claim. |
| `closeIncidentMonitoring(uint256)` |  |
| `deliverRecoveredNFT(uint256,address)` |  |
| `extensionCall(uint256,bytes)` | Extension hatch (D17 Option A). Forwards `data` to the request's pinned engine via `onExtensionCall`, appending `msg.sender` as a trailing 20 bytes so the engine can authorize per payload selector without trusting a caller-supplied argument. FwaEngineV1 reverts unconditionally; this is dead code until a future engine version implements a payload. |
| `extensionCallGlobal(bytes)` | Non-request-scoped counterpart of `extensionCall`, forwarded to `activeEngine`. Gated to registered, active application accounts, the same check `_acquire` applies. |

| `rescueNFT(address,uint256,address)` | Recovers an ERC721 mis-sent to the router. |
| `rescueToken(address,address,uint256)` | Recovers an ERC20 mis-sent to the router. The router holds no protocol funds itself; every acquisition's ETH and reward flow routes through the engine, request buyer, and reward vault instead. |

### View

| Function | Notice |
| --- | --- |
| `acquisitionReadiness()` | Acquire-pacing signals from the active engine's FWA pool, the single Midway-side read a keeper consults before requesting a new acquisition. See `FwaEngineV1.acquisitionReadiness`: a nonzero `unfulfilledVrf` means FWA's VRF subscription is under pressure and a further acquire may revert `InsufficientVrfCoverage`, so the keeper should `processAcquisitions` and wait for fulfillment rather than firing into it. |
